title: hay and estar: What There Is, and Where It Is

sections.title: hay vs estar
sections.content: Use 'hay' (there is/are) to say something exists — it never changes form, whether you mean one thing or many. Use 'estar' to say where a specific thing is: está (singular), están (plural). Rule of thumb: 'hay' introduces something new or general ('hay un café' — there's a café); 'estar' locates something you've already identified ('el café está al lado del lago' — the café is next to the lake).

items.spanish: El café está al lado del lago.
items.english: The café is next to the lake.

items.spanish: Los sábados el mercado está muy lleno.
items.english: On Saturdays the market is very crowded.

sections.content: 'Hay' comes from 'haber' and is always the same word — never say 'hays' or 'hayn'. 'Estar' does conjugate (estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están), matching the subject.
